content.text:
This docs repo covers Tailwind v4-era guidance (v3.3.3 predates `@source`), but the root cause is the same in both versions: each build (host and remote) generates its own CSS by scanning only the files it knows about — a remote's classes won't appear unless its Tailwind build actually scans that remote's source files.

- **`src/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.mdx`** ("Explicitly registering sources", section `#4`): Tailwind only generates utilities for classes it detects in the registered paths of *that* build. If your remote module is bundled separately (Module Federation style), its classes must be scanned within its own build's content globs — the host's Tailwind build won't emit CSS for the remote's classes, and vice versa.
- **`src/docs/theme.mdx`** ("Sharing across projects", `#14`): if host and remote use different `tailwind.config.js`/theme tokens, share a common theme file (or config) so generated class names/values match across builds — otherwise a class present in one build's CSS may reference a token the other doesn't have.

Practically for Nx MFE: ensure the remote's own `tailwind.config.js` `content` array covers its actual source files (not the host's), that the remote emits and loads its **own compiled CSS** at runtime (each federated module needs its Tailwind stylesheet loaded, since CSS isn't shared through the JS module federation graph), and that both configs share the same design tokens/plugins so class names resolve identically.

- **`src/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.mdx`** ("Explicitly registering sources", section `#4`): Tailwind only generates utilities for classes it detects in the registered paths of *that* build. If your remote module is bundled separately (Module Federation style), its classes must be scanned within its own build's content globs — the host's Tailwind build won't emit CSS for the remote's classes, and vice versa.
- **`src/docs/theme.mdx`** ("Sharing across projects", `#14`): if host and remote use different `tailwind.config.js`/theme tokens, share a common theme file (or config) so generated class names/values match across builds — otherwise a class present in one build's CSS may reference a token the other doesn't have.

Practically for Nx MFE: ensure the remote's own `tailwind.config.js` `content` array covers its actual source files (not the host's), that the remote emits and loads its **own compiled CSS** at runtime (each federated module needs its Tailwind stylesheet loaded, since CSS isn't shared through the JS module federation graph), and that both configs share the same design tokens/plugins so class names resolve identically.
